repository.description: Nanyang Kopi & Toast - Self-Order Kiosk, Kitchen Docket Printer & Payment POS

issues.title: Kiosk Step 2 'Kopi O Kosong' freeze & kitchen docket label coupling
issues.body:
In yesterday's Raffles Place kiosk trial, 19 of 28 first-time users (68%) froze for over 2 minutes on Step 2 ('Kopi O Kosong', 'Kopi C Siew Dai', 'Teh Halia'), and 72% missed the small top-right language toggle.

Why renaming the buttons to 'Black Coffee No Sugar' failed at Tampines:
- The kitchen docket currently prints the same name the customer sees. When English names printed on kitchen dockets at Tampines, our 65-year-old kopi uncles slowed down by 15 seconds per cup.
- POS v2.4 can hold a separate kitchen print name, but it has to be configured and kitchen-tested before the morning rush.
- The 15-inch screen only fits 12 buttons per page (about 18 characters per line). Adding two-line subtitles pushes half the drinks onto Page 2.

Not decided: which change helps a first-timer without slowing the kitchen or pushing the menu onto a second page.

issues.title: 28-seat morning crunch: tissue-packet chope-ing & laptop wall-socket campers
issues.body:
Our Raffles Place shop has only 28 seats. Between 8:00am and 10:00am, office workers leave tissue packets on empty tables before joining the 15-minute queue, while freelancers buy one $2.20 Kopi O and camp at our four 4-seater booths (16 seats) for 2 hours using the 12 wall power sockets and free Wi-Fi. That costs us about $420 every morning in lost breakfast turnover.

Floor notes from Wei Ling & Mei:
- Auntie Mary (62) got yelled at by a customer in a suit when she moved his tissue packet last week, and she will not play seat police or touch customer belongings.
- 60% of our morning customers dine solo and cannot carry a hot tray of runny soft-boiled eggs without a table.
- The 12 booth wall sockets and guest Wi-Fi router run on a programmable smart relay breaker in the back room; cutting power also affects paying customers using the sockets.

Not decided: who enforces any new seating rule, and how a solo diner with a hot tray still gets a table.

issues.title: SFA 9am food safety inspection & 58°C sous-vide egg bath dip
issues.body:
A diner from yesterday's soft trial was hospitalized with suspected salmonella (hospital lab culture takes 48 hours). Straits Times journalists arrive tomorrow at 8:00am for our ribbon-cutting, and SFA inspectors arrive at 9:00am.

Kitchen & operations constraints:
- During yesterday's 8:30am rush, our sous-vide holding bath dipped to 58°C for 45 minutes when cold eggs were added too quickly. Soft-boiled eggs require continuous 63°C holding.
- Soft-boiled eggs anchor 60% of our breakfast sets ($1,800/morning); pulling eggs completely wipes out morning set sales, while failing SFA's 9:00am swab and temperature log check triggers an immediate stop-work order.
- We have two unopened cartons of pasteurized backup eggs (Batch #405) in the storeroom that take 22 minutes per batch to heat to 63°C.

Not decided: whether to pause soft-boiled eggs or sanitize the bath and run the 63°C pasteurized backup batch with 15-minute probe logs, and what statement we give at 8:00am.

issues.title: GrabFood/Foodpanda 32% commission squeeze vs CBD corporate morning volume
issues.body:
GrabFood and Foodpanda raised breakfast commissions to 32% this week, meaning every $10 breakfast set delivered loses $0.40 after packaging. However, delivery platforms drive 50% of our morning revenue ($2,400/morning) from CBD corporate office towers.

POS, pricing & staffing constraints:
- Delisting from GrabFood/Foodpanda hands $2,400/morning in CBD office orders straight to Ya Kun.
- Raising our single-set GrabFood price by 30% to $13 triggers platform price-parity ranking penalties, though 5-set corporate bundle platters count as a separate SKU.
- Our direct web QR link has 0% commission, but only supports express self-pickup because the POS has no rider dispatch integration, and sending floor staff out as delivery runners in CBD morning traffic leaves the counter short-handed and carries injury liability.

Not decided: how we restructure our delivery menu, corporate bundles, or express self-pickup without losing CBD volume or pulling floor staff off the line.

issues.title: PayNow SGQR dynamic timeout on Kiosk #2 during concurrent checkout
issues.body:
When two customers scanned PayNow SGQR within 3 seconds on Kiosk #1 and Kiosk #2, webhook callback acknowledgements collided on the local gateway.

Resolution: Upgraded payment webhook listener to key by `terminal_id + order_seq` in POS v2.4. Verified across 50 test transactions with zero dropped receipts.

issues.title: Install 16 numbered RFID table pucks & backroom smart relay breaker for Booths 1-4
issues.body: Wired the 12 booth wall power outlets and guest Wi-Fi router to the programmable smart relay breaker in the back room, and boxed 28 numbered order buzzers/table pucks at the cashier counter ready for morning rush deployment.
